fields.quoted_span: Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).
fields.note: Eligibility (62+, permanent disability, veteran 60% disability), one-year residency before conversion recording, 40-year protection, income test, landlord notice duty and 60-day filing are all stated in the guide's Protected Tenancy section.

fields.quoted_span: Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater
fields.note: The 40 years, the 3x county average or $50,000 income limit, and the 60-day filing window ('Generally, applications for protected tenancy must be filed ... within 60 days') are all in the document.
The record's effective_date is null and the guide gives no effective date for the Act.

fields.quoted_span: The Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act protects senior citizens who meet certain eligibility requirements
fields.note: The guide describes the Act in the present tense as operative law, consistent with in_force.

fields.quoted_span: live in a building being converted to a condominium, cooperative; or fee simple ownership of units at least one (1) year prior to the conversion recording date.
fields.note: Coverage of buildings being converted, the one-year residency condition, and the age, disability and veteran eligibility and income tests are all in the document.
The guide cites N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28 for the 40-year protection and income test and gives the full range and N.J.A.C. aliases.
